nodes.label: Autoresearch
nodes.author: Andrej Karpathy
nodes.rationale: Places an agent inside an executable research harness because the output is verifiable, the action is reversible via git reset, the horizon is short (~5 min runs), and the environment is bounded.

nodes.label: AgentHub
nodes.author: Andrej Karpathy
nodes.rationale: Agent-first collaboration platform (bare Git repo, SQLite, HTTP service, CLI, message board) that removes convergence abstractions (no main branch, no PRs, no merge queue) because thousands of agents explore simultaneously and the primary operation is traversing the search graph, not merging.

nodes.label: program.md
nodes.rationale: Natural-language control spec that configures an autonomous organization; it establishes mutable/protected files, metric direction, experiment budget, run command, crash handling, commit/revert rules, and escalation policy.

nodes.label: Ratchet Loop
nodes.rationale: Iterative inspect/propose/apply/evaluate template that retains only metric improvements and reverts everything else, converting working-memory hypotheses into machine-readable experiment history.

nodes.label: Commit DAG
nodes.rationale: The DAG is literally the graph: commits are nodes, parent links are directed edges. It externalizes experiment lineage and answers 'what changed / which parent / which agent', enabling traversals (children, leaves, lineage) awkward in a branch model.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph
nodes.rationale: Shared memory layer that externalizes facts, provenance, and cross-session memory so multi-agent systems scale without copying every worker transcript into an orchestrator's context. Earns its cost only when connected queries, evolving relations, provenance, or shared world state are central.

nodes.label: Agent Swarm
nodes.rationale: Externalizes parallel search and role specialization; agents explore, implement, or evaluate concurrently and promote promising ideas to larger scales.

nodes.label: Dynamic Workflows
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Instead of a static fan-out script, Claude writes a JavaScript orchestration program that spawns fresh-context sub-agents in parallel (up to 16 concurrent, hard cap 1,000 per workflow), moving variable orchestration into generated scripts. Large fan-out is expensive (a 1,000-sub-agent high-effort run can cost tens of dollars).

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Construction Cookbook
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Replaces a classical NLP pipeline with model calls and structured schemas; the Pydantic schema is the only 'training data', collapsing trained NER and relation classifiers into one structured-output prompt per document.

nodes.label: Building Effective Agents
nodes.author: E. Schluntz, B. Zhang (Anthropic)
nodes.rationale: 2024 guidance advising teams to prefer simple, composable patterns and to begin with the simplest composable pattern.

nodes.label: Entity Resolution
nodes.rationale: Treated as a reasoning task, not string similarity, because labels can differ substantially ('Edwin Aldrin' vs 'Buzz Aldrin', zero overlap). Uses descriptions as contextual evidence and must stay additive/reversible retaining aliases, sources, and confidence, since a false merge can catastrophically contaminate many traversals.

nodes.label: Extraction (Haiku)
nodes.rationale: Schema-constrained Haiku call extracts typed entities and subject-predicate-object relations; creates surface forms, not a clean graph.

nodes.label: Graph Assembly
nodes.rationale: Property-style graph in a NetworkX MultiDiGraph storing minimum useful provenance: nodes carry type/source/count, edges carry predicate/provenance/confidence.

nodes.label: Multi-hop Querying
nodes.rationale: Should not dump the whole graph into the model: identify starting entities, traverse a bounded neighborhood, filter edges by type/date, serialize as triples, and cite edge identifiers so unsupported statements reveal the missing edge.

nodes.label: Structured Outputs (Pydantic Schema)
nodes.rationale: Model responses constrained to a Pydantic schema; the schema is the only training data and is what replaces trained NER/relation classifiers.

nodes.label: Provenance
nodes.rationale: Where a claim came from and which run produced it; every claim must have a source or be marked inference so outputs stay auditable.

nodes.label: Graph Grounding
nodes.rationale: Constraining generation with facts retrieved from a graph; a graph-grounded evaluator checks a claim against required edges and returns structured revise feedback, more actionable than free-form critique.

nodes.label: Graph as Shared Memory
nodes.rationale: Workers write findings as structured graph updates (schema+provenance validated) so a synthesizer can combine findings even if no worker saw all source documents.

nodes.label: Graph as Grounding Layer
nodes.rationale: An evaluator checks claims against graph edges; when a supporting path is missing it returns structured feedback naming the required evidence.

nodes.label: Graph as Persistent World Model
nodes.rationale: 'The agent forgets, the graph does not' - persistence enables long-running investigations, cross-session planning, incremental ingestion, contradiction tracking, audit trails, and recovery after a failed run.

nodes.label: Software 3.0 (Programming the Program)
nodes.author: Andrej Karpathy
nodes.rationale: After Software 1.0 (explicit instructions) and 2.0 (data/training), context and prompts become a programmable interface; program.md programs the program.

nodes.label: Vibe Coding
nodes.rationale: Stage 1: the human expresses intent and the model writes.

nodes.label: Agentic Engineering
nodes.rationale: Stage 2: the human specifies, orchestrates, verifies, and remains responsible for security, correctness, architecture, taste, and quality while delegating implementation to agents.

nodes.label: Graph Engineering
nodes.rationale: Stage 3: agents share durable state through typed, queryable graphs of work and knowledge; the bottleneck is the placement of memory and evaluation, not the next model call.

nodes.label: Control Plane
nodes.rationale: Receives objectives, creates plans, allocates budgets, starts workflows, and decides when to stop.

nodes.label: Execution Plane
nodes.rationale: Runs tools, tests, training jobs, code modifications, and sub-agents in isolated environments.

nodes.label: Artifact Plane
nodes.rationale: Stores plans, drafts, code changes, reports, metrics, and evaluations as immutable versions.

nodes.label: Graph Plane
nodes.rationale: Stores entities, claims, relations, provenance, experiment lineage, and task dependencies.

nodes.label: Evaluation Plane
nodes.rationale: Runs deterministic checks, model evaluators, statistical scorers, and human review; separation prevents one chat transcript from becoming database, workflow engine, and audit log.

nodes.label: Reference Production Architecture (Five Planes)
nodes.rationale: Separates control, execution, artifact, graph, and evaluation planes so no single transcript becomes the database, workflow engine, and audit log at once.

nodes.label: Graph Autoresearch (Evaluation Feedback Loop)
nodes.rationale: The evaluation harness has the same ratchet shape as autoresearch, but the artifact being optimized is the extraction prompt, ontology, resolution policy, or query serializer rather than train.py.

nodes.label: Bun Zig-to-Rust Port
nodes.author: J. Sumner
nodes.rationale: Cited as a Dynamic Workflows example: ~750,000 lines Zig to Rust in 11 days with 99.8% tests passing.

nodes.label: SETI@home
nodes.rationale: Karpathy's analogy: autoresearch should become asynchronously massively collaborative for agents, in the style of SETI@home.

nodes.label: Context Construction From a Graph
nodes.rationale: The graph must not become new context dumping; each worker gets a task-specific subgraph by resolving entities, expanding one or two hops, prioritizing recent verified claims, and serializing within a token budget with stable edge identifiers for citation.

nodes.label: Claude Haiku
nodes.rationale: Cheaper model used for schema-constrained extraction (claude-haiku-4-5).

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet
nodes.rationale: Stronger model used for entity resolution arbitration and multi-hop query reasoning.

nodes.label: NetworkX MultiDiGraph
nodes.rationale: Concrete property-graph store for assembly; nodes carry type/source/aliases, edges carry predicate/provenance/confidence.

nodes.label: Decision Framework (Six Selection Questions)
nodes.rationale: Six questions choose the architecture level: can success be verified, are steps stable, are subtasks independent, must alternative lineages remain, must facts survive the run, can the org afford cost/latency.

nodes.label: Complexity Budget
nodes.rationale: Every run declares max model calls, sub-agents, concurrent workers, tool calls, wall-clock, tokens, cost, retries, graph writes, and minimum evidence for finalization; on exhaustion return the best current artifact rather than hide partial failure.

nodes.label: Practical Build Path (Loop to Graph)
nodes.rationale: Staged path: Day 1 reflective loop, Day 2 tools, Week 1 planning, Week 2 multi-agent, Month 1 wire into a graph, Month 2 scale to a swarm - directional, not mandatory.

nodes.label: Typed Graph Schema and Invariants
nodes.rationale: Node types (Entity, Claim, Source, Artifact, AgentRun, Evaluation, Task, Commit, Metric) and edge types (MENTIONS, SUPPORTS, CONTRADICTS, DERIVED_FROM, PRODUCED, EVALUATES, REVISES, SUPERSEDES, DEPENDS_ON, PARENT_OF, RESOLVED_TO); every write satisfies four invariants (claim has source or marked inference; artifact has authoring run/version; evaluation identifies a rubric; superseded objects stay addressable).
